notes:
Top-line: building a trading assist and real-time reranking service where latency and per-token cost directly affect economics.
- Workloads: low-latency conversational agent (tile size ~200 tokens), real-time reranker on candidate lists (avg 12 candidates), and embedding compute for similarity matching.
- Targets: p95 latency <= 40ms for single-turn chat on 32 token replies; throughput target ~1k reqs/sec for reranker at peak. Very cost sensitive — target < $0.0015 per request average.
- Optimization interest: aggressive batching (dynamic batch windows), prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts, 8-bit and 4-bit quantization experiments. They asked: "Can Redwood maintain latency SLOs with quantized 4-bit models + batching?"
- Benchmark ask: want a controlled perf run across 3 configs: (1) baseline FP16 with small batching, (2) 8-bit quantized with KV cache, (3) 4-bit quantized with fallback routing. Request duration: 72h steady-state, with synthetic burst periods. Need to capture token-level cost and p50/p95/p99.
- Security & deployment: prefer VPC private control plane; may move to on-prem for final contract. KMS + audit logs mandatory. Data residency in us-east required for some trading customers.
- Procurement: legal SOW pending (finance asked for SOC2 attestation copy).
- Quote from CTO on call: "Economics matter — if the inference cost is higher than our current GPU infra we won't move. But if you can hit p95 under 40ms with the quantized profile, that's interesting."
- Internal champions: Head of infra (Sana), ML lead (Ravi) - both attended the demo.
- Risks: internal dev cycle to adapt model serving, network egress policy; heavy reliance on predictable tail latency for trading windows.
- Next: provision Dedicated test pool + run the 72h perf POC; Maya to provide RedTeam contact for KMS details.
